title: From Barren Plateaus to SPSA Optimization in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
abstract: The barren plateau (BP) phenomenon poses a fundamental challenge to the trainability of variational quantum eigensolvers (VQEs) by causing exponentially vanishing gradients as the system size increases. While extensive studies have investigated the geometric origins of BP, its impact on the optimization dynamics and complexity of practical algorithms under finite-shot measurements remains poorly understood. In this paper, we develop a theoretical framework that characterizes how the BP affects the optimization dynamics of the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA) algorithm and quantifies the resulting iteration complexity and measurement budget. We derive non-asymptotic bias and variance characterizations of the SPSA gradient estimator, introduce a signal-to-noise ratio analysis to quantify gradient reliability, and establish convergence guarantees for SPSA under finite-shot measurements. Our results show that the exponentially decaying gradient energy associated with BP leads to an exponential increase in the number of iterations required to achieve a fixed relative optimization accuracy, which in turn results in an exponential increase in the total measurement budget.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the impact of Barren Plateaus on Variational Quantum Eigensolvers optimized using SPSA. It develops statistical tools to quantify gradient estimation errors under finite measurements. The core finding demonstrates that BP causes optimization convergence to require an exponentially increasing measurement budget as system size grows.
main_problem: The paper addresses how the Barren Plateau (BP) phenomenon degrades the optimization dynamics and complexity of Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) when subjected to finite-shot measurement noise.
main_result: It is shown that the exponential decay of gradient energy due to BP forces an exponential increase in both the required number of optimization iterations and the total necessary quantum measurement budget to maintain a fixed accuracy.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework analyzing the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA) algorithm, deriving non-asymptotic bias and variance characterizations for its gradient estimator under finite measurements.
model_or_system: The study focuses on VQE applied to finding eigenvalues of a target Hamiltonian $H = \sum w_\alpha P_\alpha$ using variational parameters $	heta$. The optimization is performed on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices.
key_observables: Gradient energy decay, Signal-to-Noise Ratio ($	ext{SNR}_\ell$), required iteration count ($T$), and total measurement budget ($M$).
important_parameters: System size ($N$ or $L$), optimization step size ($\mu_t$), and the measurement shot count ($M$). The BP regime is characterized by exponential gradient decay.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a specific noise model for measurements (Lemma 1) and relies on bounding the Hessian Lipschitz constant of the VQE objective function (Proposition 1).
paper_structure: The paper builds from characterizing the BP's impact to developing statistical tools (SPSA analysis, SNR metric), culminating in convergence proofs that quantify the resource scaling required for optimization.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial theoretical bounds on the practical limitations of VQE algorithms, directly informing how quantum hardware resources (measurement time) must scale with system size when BP is present.
